To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified a common transcriptional program across lung and pancreatic cancers driven by mutant KRAS that includes the transcriptional factor FOSL.
we identified FOSL1, an oncogene that is activated by mutant KRAS, as a vulnerability for mutant KRAS-driven lung cancer and that FOSL1 inhibition impairs mutant KRAS-driven pancreatic cancer.
FOSL1 is a transcription factor that is upregulated by KRAS and promotes the growth of KRAS-mutated tumours by targeting the mitotic machinery.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel therapeutic targets in mutant KRAS lung cancers and their validation in mutant KRAS pancreatic cancer.
the identification of a transcriptional signature shared across mutant KRAS lung, pancreatic and colon cancer.
the identification of new vulnerabilities that may be exploited to develop new therapies for patients with mutant KRAS tumours.

FOSL1 is a KRAS oncogene vulnerability in lung and pancreatic cancers.
FOSL1 is an oncogene vulnerability for KRAS-driven lung or pancreatic cancer.
the FOSL1 gene is a potential therapeutic target for KRAS mutant lung and pancreatic cancers.

Fosl1 is an oncogene vulnerability for mutant KRAS lung cancer and that Fosl1 links KRAS to the mitotic machinery in a manner that can be therapeutically exploited.
